text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses training data—examples that already have correct answers—to build a model. For instance, you might show the computer thousands of photos labeled “cat” or “dog.” The model studies patterns in these examples, such as shapes or colors. Once trained, the model can make predictions on new, unseen photos. After training, we test its accuracy by checking how often its predictions match the true labels. The better the training data, the more accurate the model’s predictions become, helping us solve real-world problems like spam detection or medical diagnosis.
